main.subTitle: About Long Live Food
main.description: Eat it before your trash does

Look, we get it. Life is busy, and figuring out what to do with half a bag of spinach isn’t exactly at the top of your list. 
You may be just one smoothie away from saving a browning avocado. Or one omelette flip from rescuing half an onion. Maybe you just didn't know that herbs can last longer when stored in a cup of water, like a bouquet of flowers.

A little knowledge can go a long way toward saving food, time, and money. 
So if you want to master the art of doing a lot with a little, read on. We have all the answers you need.

You can thank us with a homemade stew.

title.copy: Most wasted food isn’t due to carelessness. Life just gets in the way.
The average American household spends about $3,000 per year on food they don’t eat.

main.description: It's rarely one bad decision. It's a bag of greens behind the milk. A jar opened for one recipe. A date label that sounds more final than it is. Most kitchens share the same handful of patterns, and most people have never had a reason to notice them. Once you see the pattern, the fixes are small, and they hold.

This site is built with WWF, WRAP, and ReFED, organizations with decades of experience in food systems and sustainability, in partnership with the Ad Council. 

Every tip is reviewed by members from these organizations and food safety experts from the Purdue University Department of Food Science, so you can trust the advice from the moment you buy an ingredient to the moment you use it.

title.copy: Built by the people who study wasted food prevention for a living

main.description:
Preventing edible food from going to waste is a great start, but peels, scraps, and shells don't have to end up in landfills either.

Composting turns scraps into something useful, and organizations across the country are working to make that easier and more accessible.

main.description:
This isn't one more thing on your plate. It’s a resource for the food you already love. Find advice on how to buy, store, use, or rescue ingredients to make the most of them. Use our tool when you know what you’re cooking, or browse the tip library whenever you've got a minute to spare.

Less waste. Less money down the drain. Less time wondering what to do next.
